permutationLabel: High surgical risk (84, CCI 8, ASA IV) — TG18 Grade II not responding to antibiotics → percutaneous drainage
summary: 84-year-old man with HFrEF (EF 25%), severe COPD and CKD 3b; 4 days of RUQ pain, fever 38.4 °C, WBC 16, CRP 230, characteristic ultrasound; still febrile after 48 h of IV co-amoxiclav.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Persistent right upper abdominal pain and fever despite antibiotics
inputs.hpi: Admitted 2 days ago with 2 days of right upper quadrant pain and fever (symptoms now 4 days). On IV co-amoxiclav for 48 hours but still febrile to 38.4°C with ongoing pain. Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 25%), severe COPD (FEV1 35%, breathless on 20 metres), CKD 3b, previous MI with stents. Charlson comorbidity index 8; anaesthetic review: ASA IV.

exam.general: Frail, breathless at rest on 2 L oxygen. Temperature 38.4°C, pulse 102/min, BP 118/64.
exam.abdomen: Right upper quadrant tenderness, positive Murphy's sign, no generalised peritonism.
exam.respiratory: Reduced air entry bilaterally with prolonged expiration.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Gallstones with a thickened 7 mm wall and pericholecystic fluid; distended gallbladder. CBD 5 mm.

comorbidities: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 25%)
inputs.socialHistory: Lives with wife. Housebound. Ex-smoker 50 pack-years.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute calculous cholecystitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute calculous cholecystitis, Tokyo (TG18) Grade II (moderate; symptoms >72 h), not responding to 48 h of antibiotics. High surgical risk (CCI 8, ASA IV): for percutaneous cholecystostomy.

recommended.note: TG18 uses CCI and ASA-PS to choose between early LC and drainage.

values.note: Duration >72 h is on its own a Grade II criterion.

mustInclude.note: TG18 Grade II, CCI ≥6 / ASA-PS ≥3, not responding to antimicrobials: urgent/early gallbladder drainage.
The Plan tab text is the documented plan; drainage must be in it, not only in the Assessment panel.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Grade I variant allows immediate/surgical/followup phases only, so "percutaneous cholecystostomy if … unfit for surgery" (conservative phase) is missing from the Plan tab; it appears only in the Assessment panel.
mustInclude.proposedFix: dx-variants.ts: include the conservative (drainage) phase in the Grade II variant, and fix variant order (see variant-grade2).

mustExclude.note: For CCI 8 / ASA IV, TG18 does not recommend early LC; an unqualified early-LC line in the plan is misleading. Quality because the plan lists options and the surgeon chooses.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Plan tab: "[surgical] Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 72 h (Grade I–II)" for a CCI 8 / ASA IV patient, with no fitness qualifier.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Cholecystitis protocol: "Early LC within 72 h if CCI ≤5 and ASA-PS ≤2 (TG18)"; add a high-risk branch "antibiotics, then PTGBD if not responding; delayed LC if fitness improves".

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

dxVariant.proposedFix: dx-variants.ts: check Grade III → II → I.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Diagnostic criteria (A local + B systemic + C imaging); Grade II: WBC >18,000/mm³, palpable tender RUQ mass, duration >72 h, marked local inflammation (gangrenous, emphysematous, abscess, biliary peritonitis); Grade III: organ dysfunction
guideline.citation: Yokoe M, Hata J, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:41–54.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — flowchart for the management of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Grade I: early LC if CCI ≤5 / ASA-PS ≤2; Grade II: early LC in an advanced centre if fit, otherwise antibiotics and urgent/early gallbladder drainage when not responding; Grade III: organ support, antibiotics, drainage unless favourable organ dysfunction
guideline.citation: Okamoto K, Suzuki K, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:55–72.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — management strategies for gallbladder drainage in acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage (PTGBD) as first-line drainage in high-risk surgical patients; acalculous cholecystitis in the critically ill
guideline.citation: Mori Y, Itoi T, Baron TH, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:87–95.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — antimicrobial therapy for acute cholangitis and cholecystitis
guideline.section: Blood cultures in Grade II/III; antimicrobial choice by severity; duration after source control
guideline.citation: Gomi H, Solomkin JS, Schlossberg D, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:3–16.

rationale: Permutation: the TG18 Grade II branch for a patient who is not fit for early surgery and is failing antibiotics. The correct plan is percutaneous gallbladder drainage with delayed cholecystectomy only if fitness improves. Tests risk-aware plan selection.
